description: Excludes the one-parameter growing-width cut of Addendum 23 Front 1 WITHOUT selecting any w. S(k)/k is increasing, so the model's per-nucleon prediction is non-decreasing in A for every fixed w; the AME per-nucleon binding is not, peaking at 4He (7.0739) and dipping at 6Li (5.3323). A non-decreasing function cannot match a function that decreases across the same two points, and an arbitrary positive rescaling preserves that -- so the failure is in the SHAPE, not the normalisation, and the family is excluded scope (b). Also corrects Addendum 23's claim that the entropy is identically zero at w = 3: S(3A) > 0 at every A, because S is a TRACE-state entropy, not a pure-state bipartition entropy (it is not even symmetric under k <-> n-k).

data.verdict: scope-(b): the one-parameter constant-w growing-width cut, and any overall rescaling of it, is excluded by the monotonicity of S(k)/k against the non-monotonicity of B/A. A cut whose width depends on the isotope's own structure is NOT excluded.
data.corrects: Addendum 23 Front 1: 'at w = 3 the cut is the entire system and the entropy is identically zero' is false; S(3A) > 0 at every A.

caveats: Scope (b) and narrow: what is excluded is the one-parameter family 'cut of width wA with w constant across isotopes', together with any overall positive rescaling of it. A cut whose width depends on the isotope's own structure is NOT excluded, and nothing here says what the missing binding term is.

No w is selected anywhere. The grid over w scans to FALSIFY a universal monotonicity claim, which is the legitimate direction; it never picks a best-scoring w. The sqrt(rmax/rmin) figure is a closed-form identity verified, not a fitted optimum.
S(k)/k is measured monotone over k = 1..64, not proved monotone for all k. The exclusion needs it only on the range the isotopes reach.
